main_text.p: XI. Longè abesse illud à tua fide & constantia; scio.
XII. Sed tamen hæc ad te vt scribam, amicorum crebræ literæ faciunt, qui de me anxij atque soliciti esse videntur.
XIII. Occurrunt & illa: facilè honestas rei causas posse obduci, sæpè, vel invitos ac repugnantes ad bellum à pacis oforibus[?] inflammari: retineri in officio difficulter milites.
XIIII. Rescribas ad hæc mihi primo quoq; tempore rogo.
XV. Nam illud leue admodum est, quod prætenditur, propterea militem conscriptum esse, vt contrà aliorum vim & iniurias agrum ille tuum defendat.
XVI. Quem enim damnum dare tibi posse censes, cùm de nostra aliorumq; vicinorum tibi fide ac beneuolentia constet?
XVII. Ego sane, vt nullius rei malæ mihi sum cõ-scius, ita minimè quoq; mihi metuo.
XVIII. Neq; accidere quicquam mihi posse vi-deo sine aliorum pernicie atque adeò Germaniæ to-tius perturbatione.

De ratione respondendi ad aliorum literas peti-torias.Atque hæc de petendi ratione breuiter sint dicta: sequitur de respondendi modo vt agamus, qui duplex est. Aut enim locum amici petitioni relinquimus: si scilicet honesta illa: si utilis: si talis extiterit, vt nō ἀ-[illegible, ~7 letters]ος esse videatur. Aut eadem reiicimus: quia,

page.notes: Left margin note beside the last paragraph is printed as "De ratione respondendi ad aliorum literas peti-torias", set over several lines in the margin. Its hyphen is the printed one at the line end. Line 13: "oforibus" is doubtful; the reading is marked [?]. Last paragraph: the Greek word after "vt nō" is only partly legible (initial ἀ- and final -ος visible); the middle is marked illegible. Long s is transcribed as s throughout; "esse" is printed as "effe" in the ligature for ss, so it is given as "esse". The page ends mid-sentence at "quia," on the last line, which is a full line; there is no catchword.
